name: Pump water
summary: Use 12V pumps made to run off a battery: RV water pumps, boat bilge pumps and car washer pumps. A small solar panel can drive a 12V pump directly while the sun shines, filling a raised tank that then feeds by gravity. Put the pump down by the water and push uphill: in practice no pump sucks water up more than about 7 m. If the source is above you, a siphon needs no pump at all.

parts.why: The pump itself: RV, bilge, washer and sump pumps
Pipe from the source to the tank; wider pipe loses less flow
Drives a 12V pump directly in sun
A raised tank stores pumped water for gravity feed
Runs the pump at night or in cloud
Float switches stop the pump when the tank is full
A check valve keeps the pipe primed when the pump stops

tips: Bilge pumps move lots of water but lose flow fast above a couple of metres of lift.
RV and boat diaphragm pumps lift higher and prime themselves; most other small pumps don’t.
Pump by day into a raised tank. A tank 3 m up gives gentle pressure all night.
Screen the intake: one leaf or pebble can wreck a small pump.

Don't pipe drinking water through ordinary garden hose: the vinyl and brass fittings can hold lead. Use hose marked "drinking water safe" or NSF/ANSI 61 (sold for RVs and boats), and run it a few seconds first.
